subject: Draft MAP milestone: Data handling acceptance criteria & dependencies
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@medrx-health.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: MAP milestone for data handling (retention/logging)

Grace — thanks again for the demo today. We covered a lot, and one of our immediate gating items for procurement is a clear MAP milestone describing data handling and compliance acceptance criteria (especially around retention, immutable audit trails, and PHI/PII controls).

Two asks from our side to help us move toward an internal approval: 
- A concise milestone statement with explicit acceptance criteria that our Security & Privacy teams can sign off on.
- Any dependencies (e.g., SOC 2 evidence, encryption KMS integration, staging env for log validation) and realistic target close date.

High-level constraints to keep in mind: MedRx requires a minimum 7-year retention window for audit logs tied to PHI-related accesses, role-based access to logs (admin-only exports), and an immutable (tamper-evident) audit trail. We also need to know whether Redwood can support token-level redaction or on-write redaction for PII fields.

Can you send a short draft MAP milestone we can attach to our procurement worksheet by EOW? If easier, a one-page acceptance-criteria list + dependency checklist will work.

Thanks — Amy
Amy Chen
Director, Compliance & Data Governance
MedRx Health

Subject: Re: Follow-up: MAP milestone for data handling (retention/logging)

Amy — appreciate the clear constraints. Draft attached: condensed MAP milestone + acceptance criteria and a dependency checklist. High-level summary below; full details in the worksheet (attached).

Draft milestone (Data handling & auditability) — acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Retention: configurable log retention with policy templates; default support for retention windows up to 10 years; policy controls scoped per-account.
- Audit trails: append-only audit logs for all model inference requests and admin actions; logs include timestamp, acting principal, request id, model version, and redaction metadata.
- Immutability: cryptographic hash chain for log batches to detect tampering (proof-of-integrity snapshots weekly).
- PHI/PII controls: on-write redaction options (pattern-based + custom rules) + token-level masking for embeddings and generation outputs.
- Access controls: role-based access control, exportability restricted to a named admin group; exports logged and require 2-step approval for PHI-containing records.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest (KMS-managed keys) and TLS 1.3 in transit.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report (redacted) and example audit log extract for a 30-day window for attestation/testing.

Dependencies we flagged:
1) Legal sign-off on PII/PHI redaction approach (you)
2) Exchange of KMS key policy / KMS onboarding (MedRx)
3) Temporary staging project to validate retention & immutability (Redwood staging env)
4) Exchange of SOC 2 artifacts or SOC 2 access window (MedRx procurement asks for this)

Target milestone close date (initial proposal): 2026-12-15. If legal review runs long, propose a contingency sprint to decouple acceptance of non-PHI items earlier (e.g., logs + retention acceptance by 2026-12-01).

Attaching: MAP-dataretention-log-audit-draft.xlsx (xlsx, 112KB) — contains a one-page acceptance criteria column, owner assignments, and checkboxes for evidence.

If that looks ok, we can update the MAP and issue a one-page signoff to attach to your procurement packet.

—Grace

Looping in a couple of clarifications from legal/security that we should bake into the MAP before sending externally:
- For PHI redaction: define the operator model (on-write vs on-read) and default to on-write where possible; show rollback/traceability for masked tokens.
- Evidence scope: MedRx asked for example audit exports showing immutability proof; we should include a short note on retention of integrity hashes and where they are stored.
- KMS: confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for the Dedicated and Private options — if not in scope for Hosted, mark as roadmap/conditional.

I've made inline edits in the attached workbook (highlighted rows) and set ownership suggestions:
- Acceptance criteria owner: Monica Patel (Redwood Security Liaison)

- Legal review owner: Marissa Cole (Legal Ops)

Thanks — the draft is heading in the right direction. Quick comments from our team (attached as inline PDF):
- Retention: confirmed requirement is 7 years for audit logs relating to PHI access; 7y is a hard regulatory expectation for certain lines of business.
- Immutability: we need to see a sample proving the append-only hash chain or alternative tamper-evidence mechanism.
- Redaction: our security team prefers on-write redaction for PHI PII, but we need documentation of the redaction rules and the ability to supply custom regex/list-based rules.
- KMS: MedRx requires customer-managed keys for production handling of PHI. Is BYOK supported for Redwood Dedicated / Private? If BYOK only for Private, we need that noted as a dependency for production.

I've attached our comments and a short checklist: MedRx_MAP_comments.pdf (pdf, 24KB). Two quick asks for timeline: if BYOK + legal sign-off can't be done by 2026-12-15, we may accept a staged acceptance where non-PHI logging and retention acceptance is signed on 2026-12-01, and PHI-specific acceptance is on 2027-01-15. Let us know feasibility.

Amy
Amy Chen
Director, Compliance & Data Governance
MedRx Health

Amy / team — thanks for the rapid feedback and the comments PDF. Quick summary of confirmed next steps and owners so we can lock the MAP in HubSpot and attach the signoff doc to the deal: 

Agreed acceptance criteria (condensed for the MAP):
- Log retention: support up to 10y; MedRx target: 7y for PHI-related audit logs. Owner: Monica Patel (security liaison). Acceptance test: confirmed export of a 30-day sample with correct fields.
- Immutability: weekly integrity snapshots using a SHA-256 hash chain persisted to an append-only store; we will provide a sample proof-of-integrity export for your review. Owner: Karthik Iyer (Platform).
- PHI/PII controls: on-write redaction available via pattern-based rules + custom rule upload; token-masking available for embeddings. Owner: Grace O'Connor (SE) for demo/test artifacts.
- KMS/BYOK: BYOK supported in Private and Dedicated offerings. For Hosted, customer-managed keys are a roadmap item — we will treat BYOK in Hosted as conditional (depends on contract). Owner: Marissa Cole (Legal Ops) to mark contractual language.
- Evidence: we will share redacted SOC 2 and a sample audit extract for a 30-day window within the next week (Monica to coordinate).

Dependencies & timeline:
- Legal review complete (Marissa) — target 2026-11-30.
- KMS policy exchange & onboarding (MedRx) — target 2026-12-05.
- Staging validation for retention + integrity tests (Redwood Platform) — target 2026-12-10.

Target close date: 2026-12-15 for non-PHI items; PHI-specific acceptance contingent on BYOK + legal sign-off, tentative 2027-01-15 if needed.

Action items (owners):
- Monica: prepare sample audit exports + integrity proof (due 2026-11-24).
- Grace: add PHI redaction sample + simple acceptance test script to the MAP (due 2026-11-22).
- Marissa: draft BYOK contractual language and SOC 2 disclosure plan (due 2026-11-30).
- Amy / MedRx: confirm acceptance of staged timeline and share KMS onboarding contact (due 2026-11-23).

I'll update the MAP in HubSpot and attach a one-page signoff for procurement once we have the above. Thanks all — we'll treat this as a high-priority MAP milestone.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
